programme: No coherent shared programme. The twelve factors split into at least four unrelated functional groups by their own target sets: an EMT/developmental cluster (SATB2 → SNAI1/SNAI2/ZEB1/CDH1/CDH2/AXIN2/LEF1/MYC/CD44/PROM1, plus TCF12, LMO4, ZBTB18, TSHZ3, SMAD6 each regulating a different corner of differentiation or smooth-muscle biology), a hematopoietic/myeloid cluster (IRF8, FOXP1, MYB, each a canonical blood-lineage regulator), a canonical E2F cell-cycle/replication cluster (E2F5 → TERT/MYC/E2F1/ASF1B/DTL), and a p53-apoptosis/inflammation cluster (ING4 → BAX/CASP3/CDKN1A/TP53/CXCL8). No target overlap, documented physical interaction, or shared pathway links these clusters to one another.
role_in_a: not applicable — no single programme spans enough of the list to assign it one role in Head and Neck Cancer
role_in_b: not applicable — no single programme spans enough of the list to assign it one role in IBS
shared_axis: None can be written honestly. Each sub-cluster is individually plausible in isolation (e.g. SATB2's EMT targets fit oral squamous carcinoma biology; IRF8/MYB/FOXP1 are lineage TFs relevant to any immune-infiltrated tissue) but nothing here ties the clusters together into one mechanism that would explain why these two specific diseases, rather than any two diseases, share it.
reasoning: Twelve factors were retrieved, but they read as four disjoint modules rather than one. Naming any one sub-cluster as 'the' programme would require silently dropping the other eight factors, which is the overgenerous move the task explicitly warns against. The retrieved literature reinforces this: where papers exist, each ties one factor to one disease in isolation (LMO4/TCF12/SMAD6/MYB/IRF8 each separately to head-and-neck carcinoma subtypes; SATB2/FOXP1 separately to gut/colon biology), with no paper connecting factors to each other.
support: PMID 12771919 — LMO4 expressed in oral squamous cell carcinoma, no IBS link. PMID 38539520 — EMT/SMAD pathway discussed in oral squamous cell carcinoma lymph-node metastasis, SMAD6 specifically not confirmed. PMID 27221705 — miR-211 represses TCF12 in carcinogen-induced oral carcinoma. PMID 37418548 — IRF8-driven dendritic reprogramming restores tumor immunogenicity, head-and-neck relevance unclear. PMID 41356463 and PMID 23598962 — MYB implicated in specific head-and-neck tumor subtypes (adnexal tumors; HPV-related adenoid cystic-like carcinoma). PMID 39716027 and PMID 28648364 — SATB2 used as a marker/driver in colon organoid differentiation protocols, not IBS-specific. PMID 41688638 — GWAS of gut microbiota composition includes loci near FOXP1, association with FOXP1 itself unconfirmed. None of these establish a cross-factor relationship.
how_to_falsify: Take the two largest candidate sub-modules — the EMT set (SATB2, TCF12, LMO4, ZBTB18, TSHZ3, SMAD6) and the lineage-TF set (IRF8, FOXP1, MYB) — and test for genomic co-occupancy (ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN in matched oral epithelium and colon epithelium/enteric tissue) or physical interaction (co-IP). Finding that two or more of these factors share binding sites at a common target set, or co-immunoprecipitate, in either tissue would overturn the 'incoherent' call and identify which sub-cluster is the real carrying module.
caveats: 184 patient-group comparisons all derive from a single independent cohort pair, so the concordance counts reflect one underlying dataset split many ways, not independent replication. Colorectal and head-and-neck epithelium are developmentally and anatomically distant tissues (endoderm-derived gut vs. ectoderm/neural-crest-derived oro-pharyngeal epithelium), which raises the bar for any single shared axis. Tissue-generic master regulators were already removed before ranking, so the absence of an obvious 'epithelial identity' TF here is by design, not an oversight. The seven single-view factors (DLX3, NHLH2, ZNF205, FOXD2, MYC, PGR, MECOM) each scored very high in one patient group but recurred in under 20% of others, confirming that high individual signal without cross-group recurrence was correctly excluded rather than folded into this account.
